22031-the-airplane-boys-among-the-clouds:
John Luther Langworthy's The Airplane Boys Among the Clouds came out in 1912, when flight was still new and dangerous. Its young heroes, the Bird boys, have spent the winter building a biplane in secret. Even their best friends were kept out of the colonel's workshop. The trial flight opens the book, and trouble follows at once.

A wreck, a rescue from the skies, and a mysterious Mr. Marsh keep the plot moving. The boys work with the local police chief against an unknown enemy. A race with a storm over Old Thunder Top caps the action. Such series books taught a generation of boys to dream in aeroplanes.
25762-billie-bradley-on-lighthouse-islan:
Janet D. Wheeler writes Billie Bradley on Lighthouse Island, or The Mystery of the Wreck, published by Cupples and Leon in 1920 with pictures. Wheeler, author of Billie Bradley and Her Inheritance and Billie Bradley at Three Towers Hall, fronts the book with girls reaching the point where the lighthouse stood.

Chapters open with lost, as a big drop splashes on Laura's nose, then a hut in the woods and ferns and mystery. Billie and her friends explore lighthouse island, chase a wreck's secret, and face storms and strangers, in a girls' series tale of courage, friendship, and detection.
britannica-1911-brynmawr:
Brynmawr is a market town of Brecknockshire, in Wales. It lies 156 miles from London by rail. Its urban district held 6833 people in 1901. This 1911 Britannica entry gives its railways and its past. A joint line links Rhymney and Abergavenny through the town. A branch runs to Pontypool. A Great Western line runs from Newport.

The town grew up around ironworks in the early 19th century. The works stood at the heads of valleys that meet nearby. The site was once called Waun Helygen, or Willow-tree Common. The Nantyglo ironworks employ many local people. The town's own coal is now exhausted. Its iron ore no longer suits modern processes. Brynmawr became a parish in 1875. It became an urban district in 1894. The district was enlarged in 1900.
